prompt: The fundamental frequency f of transverse waves on a stretched wire of length L under tension T is given by f = (1 / (2 * L)) * sqrt(T / mu), where mu is the mass per unit length of the wire. What are the SI base units of the expression sqrt(T / mu)?

answer.explanation: [T] = kg m s^-2 and [mu] = kg m^-1. Then [T / mu] = (kg m s^-2) / (kg m^-1) = m^2 s^-2. Taking the square root gives m s^-1.

distractor_explanations: s^-1 is the base unit of frequency f = (1 / 2L) * sqrt(T/mu).
Correct. [T/mu] has units m^2 s^-2, so its square root has units m s^-1 (the wave speed).
kg m^-1 is the unit of mass per unit length mu.
hints: Tension T is a force, so its base units are kg m s^-2.
Mass per unit length mu has base units kg / m = kg m^-1.
solution: sqrt(T / mu) has units sqrt((kg m s^-2) / (kg m^-1)) = sqrt(m^2 s^-2) = m s^-1.
teacher_walkthrough: Determine [T]: tension is a force, so [T] = kg m s^-2.
Determine [mu]: mass per unit length has units kg m^-1.
Evaluate quotient: [T / mu] = (kg m s^-2) / (kg m^-1) = m^2 s^-2.
Take the square root: sqrt(m^2 s^-2) = m s^-1. This represents wave speed.

provenance.independence_statement: Authored to test compound quotient and root operations on base units.
